---
title: "HDClarity: a first look"
subtitle: "Cohort, cUHDRS by HD category, CSF quality and Olink proteomics"
date: today
footer: "HDClarity: a first look"
format:
  revealjs:
    width: 1600
    height: 900
    margin: 0.06
    slide-number: c/t
    transition: none
    center: false
    embed-resources: true
    fig-dpi: 144
    fig-width: 12
    fig-height: 5.2
    fig-align: center
    include-in-header:
      text: |
        <style>
        /* Tufte palette, matching the report: paper, ink, one red accent */
        :root { --ink: #1a1a1a; --paper: #fafaf7; --rule: #d8d4cc;
                --muted: #8a857c; --secondary: #6b665d; --accent: #b3261e; }
        .reveal-viewport { background-color: var(--paper) !important; }
        .reveal { font-family: Charter, "Bitstream Charter", Georgia, serif !important;
                  color: var(--ink) !important; font-size: 30px !important; }
        .reveal h1, .reveal h2, .reveal h3 {
          font-family: inherit !important; font-weight: 400 !important;
          color: var(--ink) !important; text-transform: none !important;
          letter-spacing: 0 !important; }
        .reveal h2 { font-size: 1.45em !important; margin-bottom: 0.25em !important; }
        .reveal .why { border-left: 3px solid var(--accent); padding-left: 0.6em;
                       margin: 0.1em 0 0.4em; font-size: 0.72em; color: var(--secondary); }
        .reveal .result { border-top: 1px solid var(--rule); padding-top: 0.3em;
                          margin-top: 0.3em; font-size: 0.72em; }
        .reveal .footer, .reveal .slide-number {
          color: var(--muted) !important; background: transparent !important; }
        .reveal .callout { border-left: 3px solid var(--accent) !important;
                           background: transparent !important; }
        </style>
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
params:
  # Folder holding the HDClarity PDS4 files (profile, participation, visits,
  # csfquality, ...). No data are included in this repository.
  data_dir: "data"
  # Olink Explore 3072 data in long format, one file per matrix. Leave a
  # path empty ("") to skip that matrix; with both empty the Olink slides
  # are dropped.
  olink_csf: "data/olink_csf.csv.gz"
  olink_serum: "data/olink_serum.csv.gz"
  # Sample manifest (sample ID, subjid, visit day). Only needed when the
  # Olink files do not already carry subjid and the visit day.
  olink_manifest: "data/olink_manifest.csv"
  # "synthetic" or "real". "real" puts the data-use warning on the slides.
  data_label: "synthetic"
  # Smallest count printed in a table; smaller counts show as "<min_cell".
  min_cell: 5
  # Smallest research CAG counted as a gene carrier.
  carrier_cag_min: 40
  # Olink assays detected in fewer samples than this share are left out of
  # the association screens.
  min_detected: 0.5
  # False discovery rate for the protein screens.
  fdr: 0.05

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# The slides recompute everything from the data in `params`. All
# preparation sits in the hidden chunks at the top; the slides below only
# draw figures and write result lines.

# Base R checks the packages, because the tidyverse may be the missing one.
required_packages <- c(
  "tidyverse", "vroom", "gt", "patchwork", "ggrepel", "broom"
)
is_installed <- vapply(
  required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE
)
if (!all(is_installed)) {
  stop(
    "Install these packages before rendering: ",
    paste(required_packages[!is_installed], collapse = ", "),
    call. = FALSE
  )
}

library(tidyverse)
library(gt)
library(patchwork)
library(ggrepel)

# ragg draws sharper figures and finds system fonts; png is the fallback.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  dev = if (requireNamespace("ragg", quietly = TRUE)) "ragg_png" else "png"
)

# An empty path parameter means "skip this input".
param_path <- function(value) {
  if (is.null(value) || length(value) == 0 || is.na(value)) {
    return("")
  }
  as.character(value)
}

settings <- list(
  data_dir = param_path(params$data_dir),
  olink_paths = c(
    CSF = param_path(params$olink_csf),
    Serum = param_path(params$olink_serum)
  ),
  olink_manifest = param_path(params$olink_manifest),
  real_data = identical(params$data_label, "real"),
  min_cell = as.integer(params$min_cell),
  carrier_cag_min = as.numeric(params$carrier_cag_min),
  min_detected = as.numeric(params$min_detected),
  fdr = as.numeric(params$fdr)
)
settings$olink_paths <- settings$olink_paths[nzchar(settings$olink_paths)]

has_olink <- length(settings$olink_paths) > 0
has_both_matrices <- length(settings$olink_paths) == 2

# Olink slides are dropped from the deck when there are no Olink data.
olink_visibility <- if (has_olink) "visible" else "hidden"
pair_visibility <- if (has_both_matrices) "visible" else "hidden"

# stop() with a glue-style message: stop_with("No `{name}` file.")
stop_with <- function(...) {
  stop(str_glue(..., .envir = parent.frame()), call. = FALSE)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: read-pds
#| include: false

pds_file_names <- c(
  "profile", "participation", "visits", "assessment", "csfquality",
  "pharmacotx", "nutsuppl", "nonpharmacotx", "comorbid"
)

# The file for one PDS name: "visits.csv", or a prefixed name such as
# "hdclarity_pds4_visits.csv", optionally gzipped.
find_pds_file <- function(name, dir) {
  pattern <- str_glue("(^|_){name}\\.(csv|tsv|txt)(\\.gz)?$")
  matches <- list.files(
    dir, pattern = pattern, ignore.case = TRUE, full.names = TRUE
  )
  if (length(matches) == 0) {
    stop_with("No `{name}` file in {dir}.")
  }
  if (length(matches) > 1) {
    stop_with("More than one `{name}` file in {dir}.")
  }
  matches
}

# Files saved from Excel or written with write.csv2() can use semicolons
# and a Windows encoding. The header line decides both. Base strsplit()
# with useBytes is used because stringr refuses text that is not UTF-8.
count_fields <- function(line, delim) {
  lengths(strsplit(line, delim, fixed = TRUE, useBytes = TRUE))
}

detect_text_format <- function(path) {
  header <- readLines(path, n = 1, warn = FALSE)
  delimiters <- c(",", ";", "\t", "|")
  field_counts <- map_int(delimiters, \(delim) count_fields(header, delim))
  encoding <- if (validUTF8(header)) "UTF-8" else "windows-1252"
  list(
    delim = delimiters[which.max(field_counts)],
    locale = vroom::locale(encoding = encoding)
  )
}

# Numbers stored as text, with a decimal point or a decimal comma.
as_number <- function(text) {
  uses_decimal_comma <- any(str_detect(text, ","), na.rm = TRUE) &&
    !any(str_detect(text, fixed(".")), na.rm = TRUE)
  if (uses_decimal_comma) {
    text <- str_replace(text, ",", ".")
  }
  as.numeric(text)
}

# Every column is read as text and then typed from all rows, so a sparse
# column is not mistyped from its first few values.
read_pds_file <- function(path) {
  format <- detect_text_format(path)
  vroom::vroom(
    path,
    delim = format$delim,
    locale = format$locale,
    col_types = vroom::cols(.default = vroom::col_character()),
    na = c("", "NA"),
    progress = FALSE,
    show_col_types = FALSE
  ) |>
    readr::type_convert(na = c("", "NA")) |>
    suppressMessages()
}

if (!dir.exists(settings$data_dir)) {
  stop_with("The data folder does not exist: {settings$data_dir}")
}

pds_paths <- pds_file_names |>
  set_names() |>
  map_chr(find_pds_file, dir = settings$data_dir)

pds <- map(pds_paths, read_pds_file)
```

```{r}
#| label: check-pds
#| include: false

# The columns the slides use, by file. A release without them stops here
# with a message naming the file and the columns.
required_columns <- list(
  profile = c("subjid", "sex", "caghigh", "region"),
  participation = c("subjid", "cycle", "age", "hdcat"),
  visits = c(
    "subjid", "seq", "studyid", "visit", "visdy", "cycle", "age",
    "diagconf", "motscore", "tfcscore", "sdmt1", "swrt1", "capscore",
    "hdiss_stage_imp", "isced"
  ),
  csfquality = c(
    "subjid", "visdy", "eryflag",
    "erycnt1", "erycnt2", "erycnt3", "leukcnt1", "leukcnt2", "leukcnt3"
  )
)

check_columns <- function(data, columns, file) {
  absent <- setdiff(columns, names(data))
  if (length(absent) > 0) {
    stop_with("`{file}` lacks the column(s): {str_flatten_comma(absent)}.")
  }
}

check_unique <- function(data, keys, file) {
  repeats <- data |>
    count(across(all_of(keys))) |>
    filter(n > 1)
  if (nrow(repeats) > 0) {
    stop_with("`{file}` has repeated {str_flatten(keys, ' + ')} keys.")
  }
}

iwalk(required_columns, \(columns, file) {
  check_columns(pds[[file]], columns, file)
})
check_unique(pds$visits, c("subjid", "seq"), "visits")
check_unique(pds$participation, c("subjid", "cycle"), "participation")
```

```{r}
#| label: conventions
#| include: false

# Numeric PDS fields can hold user-defined missing codes (wrong, not
# applicable, missing, unknown), and aggregated values are text such as
# ">70".
pds_missing_codes <- c(9996, 9997, 9998, 9999)

as_capped_number <- function(x) {
  number <- readr::parse_number(as.character(x), na = c("", "NA"))
  if_else(number %in% pds_missing_codes, NA, number)
}

# HDClarity categories in disease order. These codes differ from the
# Enroll-HD hdcat codes.
hdcat_labels <- c(
  "6" = "Control",
  "1" = "Early premanifest",
  "2" = "Late premanifest",
  "3" = "Early HD",
  "4" = "Moderate HD",
  "5" = "Advanced HD",
  "8" = "Incomplete penetrance"
)

label_hdcat <- function(hdcat) {
  factor(unname(hdcat_labels[as.character(hdcat)]), levels = hdcat_labels)
}

# Composite UHDRS (Schobel et al. 2017): each part is standardised against
# the TRACK-HD reference, TMS is reversed, and the sum is shifted by 10.
# Lower is worse.
cuhdrs_terms <- function(tfc, tms, sdmt, swr) {
  tibble(
    TFC = (tfc - 10.4) / 1.9,
    `TMS (reversed)` = -(tms - 29.7) / 14.9,
    SDMT = (sdmt - 28.4) / 11.3,
    `Stroop word reading` = (swr - 66.1) / 20.1
  )
}

cuhdrs_parts <- c("TFC", "TMS (reversed)", "SDMT", "Stroop word reading")

compute_cuhdrs <- function(tfc, tms, sdmt, swr) {
  rowSums(cuhdrs_terms(tfc, tms, sdmt, swr)) + 10
}
```

```{r}
#| label: build-tables
#| include: false

# Participants ----

participants <- pds$profile |>
  transmute(
    subjid,
    sex = factor(sex, levels = c("f", "m"), labels = c("Female", "Male")),
    region,
    caghigh = as_capped_number(caghigh)
  )

# Education is copied from Enroll-HD; take each participant's first value.
education <- pds$visits |>
  mutate(isced = as_capped_number(isced)) |>
  filter(!is.na(isced)) |>
  arrange(subjid, seq) |>
  summarise(isced = first(isced), .by = subjid)

# Sampling visits ----

# TMS, CAP score, HD-ISS stage and diagnostic confidence are recorded at
# every sampling and repeat sampling visit.
sampling_visits <- pds$visits |>
  filter(studyid == "CLR", visit %in% c("Sampling", "RPT Sampling")) |>
  transmute(
    subjid,
    cycle,
    sampling_visit = visit,
    sampling_visdy = visdy,
    sampling_age = as_capped_number(age),
    sampling_tms = as_capped_number(motscore),
    capscore = as_capped_number(capscore),
    hdiss_stage = as_capped_number(hdiss_stage_imp),
    diagconf = as_capped_number(diagconf)
  )

# A package's main sampling visit: the Sampling visit, or the repeat when
# the first lumbar puncture failed.
primary_sampling <- sampling_visits |>
  arrange(sampling_visit != "Sampling", sampling_visdy) |>
  slice_head(n = 1, by = c(subjid, cycle))

# Clinical source visit ----

# TFC, SDMT and Stroop come from the package's Enroll-HD visit, or from
# the HDClarity screening when there was no Enroll-HD visit in the 90 days
# before it (PDS4 dataset structure guide, sections 3 and 8).
clinical_visits <- pds$visits |>
  filter(!visit %in% c("Sampling", "RPT Sampling")) |>
  transmute(
    subjid,
    cycle,
    source_study = studyid,
    source_visdy = visdy,
    tfc = as_capped_number(tfcscore),
    tms = as_capped_number(motscore),
    sdmt = as_capped_number(sdmt1),
    swr = as_capped_number(swrt1)
  )

# Within a package, the visit with all four cUHDRS parts that lies closest
# to the sampling visit; an Enroll-HD visit wins a tie.
source_visits <- clinical_visits |>
  drop_na(tfc, tms, sdmt, swr) |>
  inner_join(
    primary_sampling |> select(subjid, cycle, sampling_visdy),
    by = c("subjid", "cycle")
  ) |>
  mutate(gap_days = sampling_visdy - source_visdy) |>
  arrange(abs(gap_days), source_study != "ENR") |>
  slice_head(n = 1, by = c(subjid, cycle)) |>
  mutate(cuhdrs = compute_cuhdrs(tfc, tms, sdmt, swr)) |>
  select(-sampling_visdy)

# Packages ----

# One row per visit package: category and age at its screening, its main
# sampling visit and its clinical source visit.
packages <- pds$participation |>
  transmute(
    subjid,
    cycle,
    hdcat = as_capped_number(hdcat),
    group = label_hdcat(hdcat),
    age_screening = as_capped_number(age)
  ) |>
  left_join(primary_sampling, by = c("subjid", "cycle")) |>
  left_join(source_visits, by = c("subjid", "cycle")) |>
  left_join(participants, by = "subjid") |>
  left_join(education, by = "subjid") |>
  mutate(
    carrier = hdcat %in% 1:5 &
      coalesce(caghigh >= settings$carrier_cag_min, FALSE)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    package_number = dense_rank(cycle),
    packages_total = n(),
    years_since_first =
      (sampling_visdy - min(sampling_visdy, na.rm = TRUE)) / 365.25,
    .by = subjid
  ) |>
  arrange(subjid, cycle)

first_packages <- packages |>
  filter(package_number == 1)
```

```{r}
#| label: helpers
#| include: false

# Formatting, with small counts suppressed ----

format_number <- function(x, digits = 0) {
  formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
}

format_percent <- function(share) {
  scales::percent(share, accuracy = 1)
}

# A bare count, or "<min_cell" when it is small.
format_n <- function(n, min_cell = settings$min_cell) {
  if_else(
    n > 0 & n < min_cell,
    str_glue("<{min_cell}"),
    format_number(n)
  ) |>
    as.character()
}

# A count with its share, or "<min_cell" when the count is small.
format_count <- function(n, total, min_cell = settings$min_cell) {
  case_when(
    n == 0 ~ "0",
    n < min_cell ~ str_glue("<{min_cell}"),
    .default = str_glue("{n} ({format_percent(n / total)})")
  ) |>
    as.character()
}

format_median_iqr <- function(x, digits = 0) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0) {
    return("–")
  }
  quartiles <- quantile(x, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75), names = FALSE) |>
    format_number(digits)
  str_glue("{quartiles[2]} ({quartiles[1]}–{quartiles[3]})")
}

format_p <- function(p) {
  if_else(
    p < 0.001,
    formatC(p, format = "e", digits = 1),
    formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 3)
  )
}

join_with_dots <- function(texts) {
  str_flatten(texts, " · ")
}

# The result line under a figure, written from computed numbers.
show_result <- function(...) {
  cat("::: {.result}", str_c(...), ":::", sep = "\n")
}

# Groups ----

# Groups smaller than min_cell are left out of figures.
drop_small_groups <- function(data, min_cell = settings$min_cell) {
  data |>
    filter(!is.na(group)) |>
    filter(n_distinct(subjid) >= min_cell, .by = group) |>
    mutate(group = fct_drop(group))
}

# Short names: on two lines for crowded axes, on one line for text.
short_group_labels <- c(
  "Control" = "Control",
  "Early premanifest" = "Early\npre",
  "Late premanifest" = "Late\npre",
  "Early HD" = "Early\nHD",
  "Moderate HD" = "Moderate\nHD",
  "Advanced HD" = "Advanced\nHD",
  "Incomplete penetrance" = "Incomplete\npenetrance"
)

short_group_names <- short_group_labels |>
  str_replace("\n", " ") |>
  set_names(names(short_group_labels))

shorten_group <- function(group) {
  unname(short_group_names[as.character(group)])
}

# Axis labels with each group's size on the last line.
label_groups_with_n <- function(data) {
  data |>
    summarise(n = n_distinct(subjid), .by = group) |>
    arrange(group) |>
    mutate(
      short_label = short_group_labels[as.character(group)],
      label = str_glue("{short_label}\nn = {format_n(n)}")
    ) |>
    select(group, label) |>
    deframe()
}

# "Control 17.6 · Early pre 16.5 · …", for the result lines.
describe_group_medians <- function(data, value, digits = 1) {
  data |>
    filter(!is.na({{ value }})) |>
    drop_small_groups() |>
    summarise(median = median({{ value }}), .by = group) |>
    arrange(group) |>
    mutate(
      median_text = format_number(median, digits),
      text = str_glue("{shorten_group(group)} {median_text}")
    ) |>
    pull(text) |>
    join_with_dots()
}

# Figures, after Tufte ----

# Data in ink, context in grey, one red accent; no gridlines or legends;
# axes stop at the outermost breaks.
ink_colour <- "#1a1a1a"
paper_colour <- "#fafaf7"
rule_colour <- "#d8d4cc"
context_colour <- "#c8c2b5"
secondary_colour <- "#6b665d"
muted_colour <- "#8a857c"
accent_colour <- "#b3261e"

has_charter <- requireNamespace("systemfonts", quietly = TRUE) &&
  "Charter" %in% systemfonts::system_fonts()$family
report_font <- if (has_charter) "Charter" else "serif"

theme_slides <- function(base_size = 16) {
  slide_theme <- theme_minimal(
    base_size = base_size,
    base_family = report_font
  ) +
    theme(
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = paper_colour, colour = NA),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = paper_colour, colour = NA),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      panel.spacing = unit(1.2, "lines"),
      axis.line = element_line(colour = secondary_colour, linewidth = 0.3),
      axis.ticks = element_line(colour = secondary_colour, linewidth = 0.3),
      axis.text = element_text(colour = secondary_colour, size = rel(0.85)),
      axis.title = element_text(colour = secondary_colour, size = rel(0.9)),
      strip.text = element_text(colour = ink_colour, hjust = 0),
      legend.position = "none"
    )
  # A range frame: each axis line stops at its outermost breaks.
  list(
    slide_theme,
    guides(x = guide_axis(cap = "both"), y = guide_axis(cap = "both"))
  )
}

quantile_25 <- function(x) quantile(x, 0.25, names = FALSE)
quantile_75 <- function(x) quantile(x, 0.75, names = FALSE)

# A median and interquartile range in ink.
summarise_median_iqr <- function(linewidth = 0.8, size = 0.45) {
  stat_summary(
    fun = median,
    fun.min = quantile_25,
    fun.max = quantile_75,
    colour = ink_colour,
    linewidth = linewidth,
    size = size
  )
}

# One grey point per participant, with the group median and IQR.
plot_strip_by_group <- function(data, y) {
  ggplot(data, aes(x = group, y = {{ y }})) +
    geom_jitter(
      width = 0.18,
      height = 0,
      colour = context_colour,
      size = 1.1,
      alpha = 0.8
    ) +
    summarise_median_iqr()
}

# Tables ----

style_table <- function(table, font_size = 17) {
  table |>
    opt_table_font(font = c(report_font, "Georgia", "serif")) |>
    tab_options(
      table.font.size = px(font_size),
      table.font.color = ink_colour,
      table.background.color = paper_colour,
      table.border.top.color = ink_colour,
      table.border.top.width = px(1),
      table.border.bottom.color = ink_colour,
      table.border.bottom.width = px(1),
      column_labels.font.weight = "normal",
      column_labels.border.bottom.color = ink_colour,
      column_labels.border.bottom.width = px(0.5),
      table_body.hlines.color = "transparent",
      table_body.border.bottom.color = ink_colour,
      row_group.border.top.color = rule_colour,
      row_group.border.bottom.color = "transparent",
      stub.border.color = "transparent",
      data_row.padding = px(2)
    )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: clinical-results
#| include: false

# From release to analysis ----

# Participants and packages (or CSF collections) at one step.
count_step <- function(data, step, keys = c("subjid", "cycle")) {
  tibble(
    step = step,
    participants = n_distinct(data$subjid),
    packages = nrow(distinct(data, across(all_of(keys))))
  )
}

repeat_packages <- packages |>
  filter(packages_total > 1)

flow <- bind_rows(
  count_step(pds$participation, "In the release"),
  count_step(primary_sampling, "With a sampling visit"),
  count_step(
    pds$csfquality,
    "With a CSF quality record",
    keys = c("subjid", "visdy")
  ),
  count_step(source_visits, "With a complete cUHDRS"),
  count_step(repeat_packages, "With more than one package")
)

packages_per_participant <- packages |>
  distinct(subjid, packages_total)

single_package_share <- mean(packages_per_participant$packages_total == 1)

package_gaps <- packages |>
  filter(!is.na(sampling_visdy)) |>
  arrange(subjid, sampling_visdy) |>
  mutate(
    gap_years = (sampling_visdy - lag(sampling_visdy)) / 365.25,
    .by = subjid
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(gap_years))

source_summary <- source_visits |>
  summarise(
    enroll_share = mean(source_study == "ENR"),
    gap = format_median_iqr(gap_days)
  )

# cUHDRS ----

cuhdrs_first <- first_packages |>
  filter(!is.na(cuhdrs)) |>
  drop_small_groups()

control_age_rho <- cuhdrs_first |>
  filter(group == "Control") |>
  summarise(rho = cor(age_screening, cuhdrs, method = "spearman")) |>
  pull(rho)

cap_data <- first_packages |>
  filter(carrier, !is.na(cuhdrs), !is.na(capscore))

cap_rho <- cap_data |>
  summarise(rho = cor(capscore, cuhdrs, method = "spearman")) |>
  pull(rho)

# Each part's contribution to the cUHDRS difference from controls. The
# four parts add up to the whole difference.
part_contributions <- first_packages |>
  filter(!is.na(cuhdrs), hdcat %in% c(6, 1:5)) |>
  drop_small_groups() |>
  mutate(cuhdrs_terms(tfc, tms, sdmt, swr)) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(cuhdrs_parts), names_to = "part", values_to = "term") |>
  summarise(mean_term = mean(term), .by = c(group, part)) |>
  mutate(
    difference = mean_term - mean_term[group == "Control"],
    .by = part
  )

largest_drop_by_group <- part_contributions |>
  filter(group != "Control") |>
  slice_min(difference, n = 1, by = group) |>
  arrange(group)

# Repeat packages ----

repeated_cuhdrs <- packages |>
  filter(!is.na(cuhdrs)) |>
  filter(n() > 1, .by = subjid) |>
  mutate(first_group = group[which.min(cycle)], .by = subjid)

annual_change <- repeated_cuhdrs |>
  arrange(subjid, cycle) |>
  summarise(
    group = first(first_group),
    years = last(years_since_first) - first(years_since_first),
    change = last(cuhdrs) - first(cuhdrs),
    .by = subjid
  ) |>
  filter(years > 0) |>
  mutate(change_per_year = change / years)

change_by_group <- annual_change |>
  filter(!is.na(group)) |>
  summarise(
    participants = n(),
    change_per_year = median(change_per_year),
    .by = group
  ) |>
  filter(participants >= settings$min_cell) |>
  arrange(group)

# CSF quality ----

red_cell_columns <- str_c("erycnt", 1:3)
white_cell_columns <- str_c("leukcnt", 1:3)
cell_count_columns <- c(red_cell_columns, white_cell_columns)

# The mean of a triplicate count; NA when all three are missing.
mean_of_counts <- function(counts) {
  means <- rowMeans(counts, na.rm = TRUE)
  if_else(is.nan(means), NA, means)
}

csf_collections <- pds$csfquality |>
  mutate(across(all_of(cell_count_columns), as_capped_number)) |>
  transmute(
    subjid,
    visdy,
    erythrocytes = mean_of_counts(pick(all_of(red_cell_columns))),
    leukocytes = mean_of_counts(pick(all_of(white_cell_columns))),
    erythrocyte_flag = as_capped_number(eryflag) == 1
  ) |>
  left_join(
    sampling_visits |> select(subjid, visdy = sampling_visdy, cycle),
    by = c("subjid", "visdy")
  ) |>
  left_join(
    packages |> select(subjid, cycle, group),
    by = c("subjid", "cycle")
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: olink-read
#| include: false
#| eval: !expr has_olink

# Each field the slides need, with the column names it accepts: Olink's
# export name first, then janitor's snake_case. An exact match wins;
# otherwise case, spaces and punctuation are ignored.
olink_column_names <- list(
  sample_id = c("SampleID", "sample_id"),
  plate = c("PlateID", "plate_id"),
  olink_id = c("OlinkID", "olink_id"),
  assay = c("Assay", "assay"),
  panel = c("Panel", "panel"),
  npx = c("NPX", "npx"),
  lod = c("LOD", "lod"),
  sample_qc = c("QC_Warning", "qc_warning", "SampleQC", "sample_qc"),
  assay_qc = c("Assay_Warning", "assay_warning", "AssayQC", "assay_qc"),
  # optional: Olink's well type, and the plate-map link to the visit
  sample_type = c("Sample_Type", "sample_type"),
  subjid = c("subjid", "subject_id"),
  visdy = c("visdy", "visit_day")
)
optional_olink_fields <- c("sample_type", "subjid", "visdy")
manifest_column_names <- olink_column_names[c("sample_id", "subjid", "visdy")]

# The protein used as a known positive check: neurofilament light.
positive_control <- "NEFL"

simplify_name <- function(name) {
  str_to_lower(str_remove_all(name, "[^[:alnum:]]"))
}

# The file's column for each field (named field = column).
match_columns <- function(available, accepted, file, optional = character()) {
  pick_column <- function(candidates) {
    exact <- intersect(candidates, available)
    loose <- available[simplify_name(available) %in% simplify_name(candidates)]
    c(exact, loose, NA_character_)[1]
  }
  found <- map_chr(accepted, pick_column)
  absent <- setdiff(names(found)[is.na(found)], optional)
  if (length(absent) > 0) {
    stop_with(
      "`{file}` has no column for: {str_flatten_comma(absent)}. ",
      "Its columns are: {str_flatten_comma(available)}."
    )
  }
  found[!is.na(found)]
}

# Only the needed columns are read: the Olink files are several hundred
# megabytes each.
read_columns <- function(path, accepted, optional = character()) {
  format <- detect_text_format(path)
  header <- vroom::vroom(
    path,
    delim = format$delim,
    locale = format$locale,
    n_max = 0,
    show_col_types = FALSE,
    progress = FALSE
  ) |>
    names()
  columns <- match_columns(header, accepted, basename(path), optional)

  vroom::vroom(
    path,
    delim = format$delim,
    locale = format$locale,
    col_select = all_of(columns),
    col_types = vroom::cols(.default = vroom::col_character()),
    na = c("", "NA"),
    progress = FALSE,
    show_col_types = FALSE
  ) |>
    mutate(across(any_of(c("npx", "lod", "visdy")), as_number))
}

# One matrix in a common shape. Participant samples are the SAMPLE wells
# when Olink's well type is present, otherwise the rows linked to a
# participant (control wells have none).
read_olink_matrix <- function(path, manifest) {
  values <- read_columns(path, olink_column_names, optional_olink_fields)

  if (!all(c("subjid", "visdy") %in% names(values))) {
    if (is.null(manifest)) {
      stop_with(
        "`{basename(path)}` has no subjid and visit day, ",
        "and no manifest was given."
      )
    }
    values <- values |>
      select(-any_of(c("subjid", "visdy"))) |>
      left_join(manifest, by = "sample_id")
  }

  has_well_type <- "sample_type" %in% names(values)
  values |>
    mutate(
      is_sample = if (has_well_type) sample_type == "SAMPLE" else !is.na(subjid)
    ) |>
    select(-any_of("sample_type"))
}

walk(settings$olink_paths, \(path) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) stop_with("Olink file not found: {path}")
})

manifest <- if (nzchar(settings$olink_manifest)) {
  read_columns(settings$olink_manifest, manifest_column_names)
}

olink <- settings$olink_paths |>
  imap(\(path, matrix) {
    read_olink_matrix(path, manifest) |>
      mutate(matrix = matrix, .before = 1)
  }) |>
  list_rbind()
```

```{r}
#| label: olink-link
#| include: false
#| eval: !expr has_olink

# Each sample's participant and sampling-visit day, then that visit's
# package. A sample run on several plates keeps its first plate.
sample_info <- olink |>
  filter(is_sample) |>
  summarise(plate = first(plate), .by = c(matrix, sample_id, subjid, visdy))

linked_samples <- sample_info |>
  left_join(
    sampling_visits |>
      select(subjid, visdy = sampling_visdy, cycle, sampling_age),
    by = c("subjid", "visdy")
  )

# One sample per participant and matrix: the earliest.
olink_samples <- linked_samples |>
  filter(!is.na(cycle)) |>
  slice_min(visdy, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE, by = c(subjid, matrix)) |>
  left_join(
    packages |> select(subjid, cycle, hdcat, group, carrier, cuhdrs, sex),
    by = c("subjid", "cycle")
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: olink-quality
#| include: false
#| eval: !expr has_olink

# Olink flags are PASS or WARN (FAIL in newer exports); an empty flag is
# not a warning.
is_warning <- function(flag) {
  !is.na(flag) & toupper(flag) != "PASS"
}

olink_samples_only <- olink |>
  filter(is_sample)

# Samples and assays that passed Olink's QC. Values below the LOD stay in,
# as Olink advises.
olink_clean <- olink_samples_only |>
  filter(!is_warning(sample_qc), !is_warning(assay_qc), !is.na(npx))

detection <- olink_clean |>
  filter(!is.na(lod)) |>
  summarise(
    detected = mean(npx >= lod),
    .by = c(matrix, olink_id, assay, panel)
  )

kept_assays <- detection |>
  filter(detected >= settings$min_detected)

# The overview table, built from one summary per question.
sample_links <- linked_samples |>
  summarise(
    samples = n(),
    linked = sum(!is.na(cycle)),
    participants = n_distinct(subjid[!is.na(cycle)]),
    .by = matrix
  )

sample_warnings <- olink_samples_only |>
  distinct(matrix, sample_id, panel, sample_qc) |>
  summarise(sample_warnings = mean(is_warning(sample_qc)), .by = matrix)

lod_summary <- olink_samples_only |>
  filter(!is.na(npx), !is.na(lod)) |>
  summarise(
    below_lod = mean(npx < lod),
    assays = n_distinct(olink_id),
    .by = matrix
  )

olink_overview <- sample_links |>
  left_join(sample_warnings, by = "matrix") |>
  left_join(lod_summary, by = "matrix") |>
  left_join(count(kept_assays, matrix, name = "assays_kept"), by = "matrix")

# Analysis values: QC-passed values of the analysed samples, replicate
# wells averaged, and the assays kept for the screens.
olink_values <- olink_clean |>
  select(matrix, sample_id, olink_id, assay, panel, npx) |>
  inner_join(
    olink_samples |>
      select(
        matrix, sample_id, subjid, group, hdcat, carrier, cuhdrs, sex,
        age = sampling_age
      ),
    by = c("matrix", "sample_id")
  ) |>
  summarise(
    npx = mean(npx),
    .by = c(
      matrix, subjid, sample_id, olink_id, assay, panel,
      group, hdcat, carrier, cuhdrs, sex, age
    )
  )

olink_analysis <- olink_values |>
  semi_join(kept_assays, by = c("matrix", "olink_id"))

nefl <- olink_values |>
  filter(assay == positive_control)
```

```{r}
#| label: olink-batch
#| include: false
#| eval: !expr has_olink

fill_with_median <- function(values) {
  coalesce(values, median(values, na.rm = TRUE))
}

is_varying <- function(values) {
  is.numeric(values) && sd(values) > 0
}

# PCA needs a complete samples × assays matrix: missing values are filled
# with the assay's median, and constant assays are dropped.
run_pca <- function(long_values, n_components = 5) {
  wide_values <- long_values |>
    select(sample_id, olink_id, npx) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = olink_id, values_from = npx) |>
    mutate(across(-sample_id, fill_with_median)) |>
    select(sample_id, where(is_varying))

  pca <- wide_values |>
    select(-sample_id) |>
    prcomp(scale. = TRUE)

  scores <- pca$x[, seq_len(n_components)] |>
    as_tibble() |>
    rename_with(str_to_lower)

  list(
    scores = bind_cols(select(wide_values, sample_id), scores),
    variance = (pca$sdev^2 / sum(pca$sdev^2))[seq_len(n_components)]
  )
}

pca_by_matrix <- olink_analysis |>
  nest(.by = matrix) |>
  mutate(pca = map(data, run_pca))

pca_scores <- pca_by_matrix |>
  transmute(matrix, scores = map(pca, "scores")) |>
  unnest(scores) |>
  left_join(
    olink_samples |>
      select(matrix, sample_id, subjid, plate, group, sex, age = sampling_age),
    by = c("matrix", "sample_id")
  )

batch_factors <- c("plate", "group", "sex", "age")

# R² of one component's scores on one factor.
r_squared_on <- function(scores, factor_name) {
  data <- scores |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[factor_name]]))
  if (n_distinct(data[[factor_name]]) < 2) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  fit <- lm(reformulate(factor_name, response = "score"), data = data)
  summary(fit)$r.squared
}

r_squared_by_factor <- function(scores) {
  batch_factors |>
    set_names() |>
    map_dbl(\(factor_name) r_squared_on(scores, factor_name))
}

batch_table <- pca_scores |>
  pivot_longer(
    starts_with("pc"),
    names_to = "component",
    values_to = "score"
  ) |>
  nest(.by = c(matrix, component)) |>
  mutate(r_squared = map(data, r_squared_by_factor)) |>
  select(-data) |>
  unnest_wider(r_squared)

# The largest R² of each factor over the first five components.
batch_summary <- batch_table |>
  summarise(
    across(c(plate, group, age), \(r_squared) max(r_squared, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .by = matrix
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: olink-differential
#| include: false
#| eval: !expr has_olink

# Carriers against controls: one linear model per protein, adjusted for
# age and sex. Incomplete penetrance is left out.
fit_carrier_difference <- function(data) {
  lm(npx ~ carrier + age + sex, data = data) |>
    broom::tidy() |>
    filter(term == "carrierTRUE") |>
    select(estimate, p.value)
}

differential <- olink_analysis |>
  filter(carrier | hdcat == 6, !is.na(age), !is.na(sex)) |>
  nest(.by = c(matrix, olink_id, assay, panel)) |>
  mutate(fit = map(data, fit_carrier_difference)) |>
  select(-data) |>
  unnest(fit) |>
  mutate(p_fdr = p.adjust(p.value, method = "BH"), .by = matrix)

differential_counts <- differential |>
  summarise(
    tested = n(),
    higher = sum(p_fdr < settings$fdr & estimate > 0),
    lower = sum(p_fdr < settings$fdr & estimate < 0),
    strongest = assay[which.min(p.value)],
    .by = matrix
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: olink-cuhdrs
#| include: false
#| eval: !expr has_olink

# Ranks of a variable with the covariates' linear effect removed.
rank_residuals <- function(values, covariates) {
  residuals(lm(rank(values) ~ ., data = covariates))
}

# Partial Spearman correlation of a protein with cUHDRS: the correlation
# of rank residuals once the rank of age (and sex) are removed from both.
partial_spearman <- function(data) {
  covariates <- data |>
    transmute(age_rank = rank(age), sex) |>
    select(where(\(values) n_distinct(values) > 1))

  rho <- cor(
    rank_residuals(data$npx, covariates),
    rank_residuals(data$cuhdrs, covariates)
  )
  df <- nrow(data) - 2 - ncol(covariates)
  t_statistic <- rho * sqrt(df / (1 - rho^2))

  tibble(n = nrow(data), rho = rho, p.value = 2 * pt(-abs(t_statistic), df))
}

cuhdrs_associations <- olink_analysis |>
  filter(carrier, !is.na(cuhdrs), !is.na(age), !is.na(sex)) |>
  nest(.by = c(matrix, olink_id, assay, panel)) |>
  mutate(fit = map(data, partial_spearman)) |>
  select(-data) |>
  unnest(fit) |>
  mutate(p_fdr = p.adjust(p.value, method = "BH"), .by = matrix)

cuhdrs_counts <- cuhdrs_associations |>
  summarise(
    tested = n(),
    passing = sum(p_fdr < settings$fdr),
    carriers = max(n),
    .by = matrix
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: olink-csf-serum
#| include: false
#| eval: !expr has_both_matrices

# A correlation needs enough participants with both samples to mean much.
min_paired_participants <- 10
strong_correlation <- 0.5

csf_serum <- olink_analysis |>
  select(matrix, subjid, olink_id, assay, npx) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = matrix, values_from = npx) |>
  drop_na(CSF, Serum) |>
  summarise(
    rho = cor(CSF, Serum, method = "spearman"),
    participants = n(),
    .by = c(olink_id, assay)
  ) |>
  filter(participants >= min_paired_participants)
```

## About these data

```{r}
#| label: data-status
#| results: asis

# Quarto does not evaluate R inside the YAML footer, so the data status is
# appended to the footer of every slide with a style rule instead.
data_status <- if (settings$real_data) {
  "Contains HDClarity data · do not share outside the data use agreement"
} else {
  "Synthetic data · no real participant data"
}
footer_rule <- '.reveal .footer p::after {{ content: " · {data_status}"; }}'
cat("<style>", str_glue(footer_rule), "</style>")
```

```{r}
#| label: status-callout
#| results: asis
if (settings$real_data) {
  cat(
    "::: {.callout-warning}",
    "## Contains HDClarity data",
    "Rendered on data released under the HDClarity data use agreement.",
    "Do not publish these slides. Counts below the small-cell threshold",
    str_glue("show as \"<{settings$min_cell}\", and groups that small are"),
    "left out of figures.",
    ":::",
    sep = "\n"
  )
} else {
  cat(
    "::: {.callout-important}",
    "## Synthetic data only",
    "Built only from publicly available HDClarity and Enroll-HD documentation.",
    "**No real participant data were used, seen or summarised**; no",
    "number here is a finding about HD.",
    ":::",
    sep = "\n"
  )
}
```

- **Scope:** the HDClarity release only, meaning the PDS4 files plus the Olink Explore 3072
  biosample data. The Enroll-HD visits packaged inside HDClarity are part of that release, and
  they hold most clinical scores.
- **Statistics:** deliberately simple. Counts, medians, Spearman correlations, and linear models
  adjusted for age and sex.
- **Status:** a first look to see what the data can support, not confirmatory testing.

::: {.notes}
HDClarity is a CSF biobank study on the Enroll-HD platform. Participants have a yearly screening
visit and a fasted sampling visit with a lumbar puncture and a blood draw. Clinical scales are
mostly taken from the Enroll-HD visit in the same year, which is why those rows stay in.
:::

## Four questions

1. **What is in the data?** Files, participants, visit packages and samples.
2. **Who is in it?** The cohort by HDClarity category.
3. **How does cUHDRS vary** with category, age, CAP score and stage, and which of its parts
   drive the differences?
4. **What do the biosamples look like?** CSF quality, then Olink: quality, batch, carriers
   against controls, proteins that track cUHDRS, and CSF against serum.

::: {.notes}
Each analysis slide has three parts. The **why** line gives the reason for the analysis, the
figure or table shows the result, and the line at the bottom gives the numbers, computed from
whichever release the deck was rendered on.
:::

# The data

## How a sample links to clinical data

::: {.why}
**Why:** every later analysis pairs a biosample with clinical scores. In HDClarity that link
runs through the *visit package*, so it has to be understood first.
:::

```{r}
#| label: visits-table
visit_roles <- c(
  "Screening" = "Eligibility; clinical scales if no recent Enroll-HD visit",
  "Sampling" = "Lumbar puncture and blood draw within 30 days; TMS",
  "RPT Sampling" = "Optional repeat 4–8 weeks later (first year only)",
  "Baseline" = "Enroll-HD visit up to 90 days before; most clinical scales",
  "Follow Up" = "Enroll-HD visit up to 90 days before; most clinical scales"
)

pds$visits |>
  count(studyid, visit) |>
  mutate(
    role = visit_roles[visit],
    n = format_n(n)
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    studyid = "Study",
    visit = "Visit",
    n = "Visits",
    role = "Role in the package"
  ) |>
  style_table(font_size = 20)
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
show_result(
  str_glue("{format_n(nrow(pds$participation))} visit packages from "),
  str_glue("{format_n(n_distinct(pds$participation$subjid))} participants. "),
  "Visits in one package share a `cycle` number."
)
```

::: {.notes}
From the PDS4 dataset structure guide, sections 3 and 8:

- A plate map gives each sample's subjid and the visdy of its sampling visit.
- That finds the sampling row, and its `cycle` finds the screening and Enroll-HD visits of the
  same package.
- A package enters the release only if at least one CSF sample was collected successfully.
:::

## How many participants each analysis can use

::: {.why}
**Why:** losses between steps set the size of every later analysis and show where data are
missing by design.
:::

```{r}
#| label: flow-table
flow |>
  mutate(across(c(participants, packages), format_n)) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    step = "",
    participants = "Participants",
    packages = "Packages or collections"
  ) |>
  style_table(font_size = 22)
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
single_share_text <- format_percent(single_package_share)
gap_text <- format_median_iqr(package_gaps$gap_years, digits = 1)
show_result(
  str_glue("{single_share_text} of participants have a single package; "),
  str_glue("consecutive packages are a median {gap_text} years apart.")
)
```

::: {.notes}
A complete cUHDRS needs all four parts (TFC, TMS, SDMT and Stroop word reading) at one visit.
Most participants have only one package, so the data are mainly cross-sectional, and that
shapes everything that follows.
:::

# Who is in the cohort

## The cohort by HDClarity category {.scrollable}

::: {.why}
**Why:** the categories are defined by protocol (CAG, burden of pathology, motor diagnosis,
TFC). Describing them checks they differ as intended and shows what each group brings, such as
age differences that later analyses must adjust for.
:::

```{r}
#| label: cohort-table
regions <- sort(unique(na.omit(first_packages$region)))

# One column of the cohort table: a group's characteristics as text.
describe_group <- function(data) {
  n <- nrow(data)
  count_of <- function(condition) format_count(sum(condition, na.rm = TRUE), n)

  demographics <- tribble(
    ~characteristic, ~value,
    "Participants", format_n(n),
    "Female", count_of(data$sex == "Female"),
    "Age, years", format_median_iqr(data$age_screening),
    "CAG", format_median_iqr(data$caghigh),
    "CAP score", format_median_iqr(data$capscore),
    "Tertiary education", count_of(data$isced >= 5)
  )
  region_rows <- tibble(
    characteristic = regions,
    value = map_chr(regions, \(region) count_of(data$region == region))
  )
  scores <- tribble(
    ~characteristic, ~value,
    "TMS", format_median_iqr(data$tms),
    "TFC", format_median_iqr(data$tfc),
    "SDMT", format_median_iqr(data$sdmt),
    "Stroop word reading", format_median_iqr(data$swr),
    "cUHDRS", format_median_iqr(data$cuhdrs, digits = 1)
  )

  rows <- bind_rows(demographics, region_rows, scores)
  # a group too small to describe keeps only its (suppressed) size
  if (n < settings$min_cell) {
    rows$value[-1] <- "–"
  }
  rows
}

first_packages |>
  filter(!is.na(group)) |>
  nest(.by = group) |>
  arrange(group) |>
  mutate(
    summary = map(data, describe_group),
    group = shorten_group(group)
  ) |>
  select(group, summary) |>
  unnest(summary) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = value) |>
  gt(rowname_col = "characteristic") |>
  style_table(font_size = 19)
```

::: {.notes}
- **Which package:** each participant at their first visit package. Median (interquartile range)
  or count (%).
- **Category definitions:**
  - Pre-manifest carriers have CAG ≥ 40 and no motor diagnosis. They are split by burden,
    (CAG − 35.5) × age, below or at least 250.
  - Manifest carriers are split by TFC: 7–13, 3–6 and 0–2.
  - Incomplete penetrance means CAG 36–39.
- **CAP score** is age × (CAG − 30) / 6.49, a different scale from the burden score.
- **hdcat** is reviewed at screenings 1 and 5 and carried forward between them.
:::

## HDClarity category against HD-ISS stage

::: {.why}
**Why:** the categories mix burden, motor diagnosis and function. HD-ISS (Tabrizi et al. 2022)
stages biology and function on one scale. Seeing how they overlap shows how mixed each category
is.
:::

```{r}
#| label: hdiss-table
first_packages |>
  filter(!is.na(group)) |>
  mutate(
    stage = if_else(
      is.na(hdiss_stage),
      "Not staged",
      str_glue("Stage {hdiss_stage}")
    )
  ) |>
  count(group, stage) |>
  mutate(n = format_n(n)) |>
  arrange(stage) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = stage, values_from = n, values_fill = "0") |>
  arrange(group) |>
  gt(rowname_col = "group") |>
  style_table(font_size = 22)
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
staged_premanifest <- first_packages |>
  filter(hdcat %in% c(1, 2), !is.na(hdiss_stage))

stage_2_or_3_share <- mean(staged_premanifest$hdiss_stage >= 2)

show_result(
  format_percent(stage_2_or_3_share),
  " of staged pre-manifest carriers are already in HD-ISS stage 2 or 3."
)
```

::: {.notes}
HD-ISS stages:

- stage 0: CAG ≥ 40 only;
- stage 1: biomarker change (caudate or putamen volume);
- stage 2: clinical signs (motor or cognitive);
- stage 3: functional decline.

The release imputes the stage for CAG 40–50 only, so controls, incomplete penetrance and
CAG > 50 are "not staged".
:::

# cUHDRS

## How cUHDRS is built here

::: {.why}
**Why:** cUHDRS combines four scales into one score that is more sensitive to change than any
single scale (Schobel et al. 2017). In HDClarity its parts sit on different visits, so the
pairing rule has to be explicit.
:::

$$
\text{cUHDRS} = \frac{\text{TFC} - 10.4}{1.9} - \frac{\text{TMS} - 29.7}{14.9} + \frac{\text{SDMT} - 28.4}{11.3} + \frac{\text{SWR} - 66.1}{20.1} + 10
$$

- **Sampling visit:** records TMS only.
- **The other three scales:** come from the package's Enroll-HD visit, or from the HDClarity
  screening when no Enroll-HD visit fell in the previous 90 days.
- **Pairing rule:** within each package, use the visit with all four parts that lies closest to
  the sampling visit.

```{r}
#| results: asis
enroll_share_text <- format_percent(source_summary$enroll_share)
show_result(
  str_glue("{format_n(nrow(source_visits))} packages have a complete cUHDRS; "),
  str_glue("{enroll_share_text} come from an Enroll-HD visit, "),
  str_glue("a median {source_summary$gap} days before sampling.")
)
```

::: {.notes}
The weights standardise each scale against the TRACK-HD reference and reverse TMS so that lower
is worse for every part. A healthy adult scores about 17–18, and the score falls as HD
progresses. Using all four parts from one visit keeps the composite internally consistent.
:::

## How does cUHDRS differ across categories?

::: {.why}
**Why:** cUHDRS is the outcome for every biomarker comparison. It should separate the
categories it is meant to reflect, and the overlap between them shows how much it adds beyond
the category label.
:::

```{r}
#| label: cuhdrs-group-figure
#| fig-height: 4.6
plot_strip_by_group(cuhdrs_first, cuhdrs) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = label_groups_with_n(cuhdrs_first)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "cUHDRS") +
  theme_slides()
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
show_result("Median cUHDRS: ", describe_group_medians(cuhdrs_first, cuhdrs))
```

::: {.notes}
Each participant at their first package. The grey points are participants, and the black mark is
the median with its interquartile range. Groups smaller than the small-cell threshold are left
out.
:::

## Is the difference just age?

::: {.why}
**Why:** age lowers cognitive scores even without HD, and the categories differ in age. Plotting
against age shows whether a category's position is explained by how old its members are.
:::

```{r}
#| label: cuhdrs-age-figure
#| fig-height: 4.8
everyone <- cuhdrs_first |>
  select(-group)

ggplot(cuhdrs_first, aes(x = age_screening, y = cuhdrs)) +
  geom_point(data = everyone, colour = rule_colour, size = 0.6) +
  geom_point(colour = ink_colour, size = 0.9, alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(
    vars(group),
    nrow = 2,
    labeller = as_labeller(short_group_names)
  ) +
  labs(x = "Age at screening, years", y = "cUHDRS") +
  theme_slides(base_size = 15)
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
show_result(
  "In controls, the Spearman correlation of cUHDRS with age is ",
  str_glue("{format_number(control_age_rho, digits = 2)}.")
)
```

::: {.notes}
Each panel shows one category in black, with everyone else in grey for context. The correlation
in controls gives the age effect without HD, which sets the baseline against which carriers are
judged.
:::

## Does cUHDRS track expected disease burden?

::: {.why}
**Why:** the CAP score combines CAG and age into expected progression; 100 is roughly the
expected age at motor diagnosis. If cUHDRS falls steadily with CAP in carriers, it measures the
disease continuously, not just by category.
:::

```{r}
#| label: cuhdrs-cap-figure
#| fig-height: 4.6
ggplot(cap_data, aes(x = capscore, y = cuhdrs)) +
  geom_point(colour = ink_colour, size = 1, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "loess",
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = FALSE,
    colour = accent_colour,
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  labs(x = "CAP score", y = "cUHDRS") +
  theme_slides()
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
cap_rho_text <- format_number(cap_rho, digits = 2)
show_result(
  str_glue("Carriers: n = {format_n(nrow(cap_data))}; "),
  str_glue("Spearman correlation with CAP {cap_rho_text}.")
)
```

::: {.notes}
CAP = age × (CAG − 30) / 6.49 (Warner et al.). The red line is a loess smooth. A bend in the
smooth suggests cUHDRS changes little early and faster later, which is the pattern expected from
natural-history studies.
:::

## Which parts drive the differences?

::: {.why}
**Why:** two groups can share a cUHDRS for different reasons. Splitting the difference from
controls into its four parts shows whether function, motor or cognition dominates at each stage.
:::

```{r}
#| label: cuhdrs-parts-figure
#| fig-height: 4.6
most_advanced_group <- last(levels(fct_drop(part_contributions$group)))
part_labels <- part_contributions |>
  filter(group == most_advanced_group)

ggplot(part_contributions, aes(x = group, y = difference, group = part)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = rule_colour) +
  geom_line(colour = ink_colour, linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(colour = ink_colour, size = 1.8) +
  geom_text_repel(
    aes(label = part),
    data = part_labels,
    nudge_x = 0.25,
    hjust = 0,
    direction = "y",
    size = 5,
    family = report_font,
    colour = ink_colour,
    segment.colour = rule_colour
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = short_group_labels,
    expand = expansion(add = c(0.4, 1.8))
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Difference from controls,\ncUHDRS units") +
  theme_slides()
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
largest_drop_texts <- str_glue(
  "{shorten_group(largest_drop_by_group$group)} {largest_drop_by_group$part}"
)
show_result("Largest drop: ", join_with_dots(largest_drop_texts))
```

::: {.notes}
Each part's term from the cUHDRS formula is averaged per category, and the control mean is
subtracted. The four lines add up to the category's cUHDRS difference from controls. TFC has a
ceiling at 13, so it moves only once function declines; cognition often moves earlier.
:::

## What do repeat packages show?

::: {.why}
**Why:** before planning longitudinal biomarker work, check how many participants have repeated
measures and over what span. The change per year is a feasibility check, not an estimate of
progression.
:::

```{r}
#| label: cuhdrs-change-figure
#| fig-height: 4.4
repeated_by_first_group <- repeated_cuhdrs |>
  mutate(group = first_group) |>
  drop_small_groups()

if (nrow(repeated_by_first_group) > 0) {
  ggplot(
    repeated_by_first_group,
    aes(x = years_since_first, y = cuhdrs, group = subjid)
  ) +
    geom_line(colour = ink_colour, linewidth = 0.35, alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_point(colour = ink_colour, size = 0.6) +
    facet_wrap(
      vars(group),
      nrow = 2,
      labeller = as_labeller(short_group_names)
    ) +
    labs(x = "Years since first sampling visit", y = "cUHDRS") +
    theme_slides(base_size = 15)
}
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
change_texts <- str_glue(
  "{shorten_group(change_by_group$group)} ",
  "{format_number(change_by_group$change_per_year, digits = 2)}"
)
follow_up_text <- format_number(median(annual_change$years), digits = 1)
show_result(
  str_glue("{format_n(nrow(annual_change))} participants with repeats "),
  str_glue("(median follow-up {follow_up_text} years). "),
  "Median change per year: ",
  join_with_dots(change_texts)
)
```

::: {.notes}
Change per year is (last − first cUHDRS) divided by the years between them, per participant.
Over one or two years measurement noise is large compared with true change, so these medians
show feasibility only.
:::

# Biosamples

## Are the CSF samples clean?

::: {.why}
**Why:** blood in CSF carries plasma proteins into the sample and can mimic or hide a CSF
signal. Red-cell counts are the first quality check before any CSF biomarker analysis.
:::

```{r}
#| label: csf-red-cells-figure
#| fig-height: 4.4
red_cells_by_group <- csf_collections |>
  filter(!is.na(erythrocytes)) |>
  drop_small_groups()

plot_strip_by_group(red_cells_by_group, erythrocytes) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    transform = scales::pseudo_log_trans(sigma = 1, base = 10),
    breaks = c(0, 10, 100, 1000, 10000),
    labels = scales::label_comma()
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = label_groups_with_n(red_cells_by_group)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Red cells per µl") +
  theme_slides()
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
collections <- nrow(csf_collections)
flagged_collections <- sum(csf_collections$erythrocyte_flag, na.rm = TRUE)
red_cells_text <- format_median_iqr(csf_collections$erythrocytes, digits = 1)
show_result(
  str_glue("{format_n(collections)} collections; "),
  str_glue("median {red_cells_text} red cells per µl; "),
  str_glue("red-cell flag on {format_count(flagged_collections, collections)}.")
)
```

::: {.notes}
Cells are counted three times per µl at the site within an hour of collection, and the plot
shows the mean of the three on a pseudo-log scale. If red-cell counts differ by category,
contamination could confound protein differences, so it is worth adjusting for or excluding
heavily contaminated samples.
:::

## Are the Olink data fit for analysis? {visibility="`r olink_visibility`"}

::: {.why}
**Why:** before any biology, check three things: the samples link to clinical visits, Olink's
own QC flags are rare, and enough assays are detected above the limit of detection (LOD).
:::

```{r}
#| label: olink-overview-table
#| eval: !expr has_olink
olink_overview |>
  select(
    matrix, samples, linked, participants,
    sample_warnings, below_lod, assays, assays_kept
  ) |>
  gt(rowname_col = "matrix") |>
  cols_label(
    samples = "Samples",
    linked = "Linked",
    participants = "Participants",
    sample_warnings = "QC warnings",
    below_lod = "Below LOD",
    assays = "Assays",
    assays_kept = "Assays kept"
  ) |>
  fmt_percent(c(sample_warnings, below_lod), decimals = 1) |>
  fmt_number(
    c(samples, linked, participants, assays, assays_kept),
    decimals = 0
  ) |>
  style_table(font_size = 22)
```

```{r}
#| label: olink-detection-figure
#| eval: !expr has_olink
#| fig-height: 3.2
panel_detection <- detection |>
  summarise(detected = median(detected), .by = c(matrix, panel)) |>
  mutate(panel = fct_reorder(panel, detected, .fun = min))

top_panel_labels <- panel_detection |>
  filter(panel == last(levels(panel)))

ggplot(panel_detection, aes(x = detected, y = panel)) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = settings$min_detected,
    colour = accent_colour,
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_line(aes(group = panel), colour = rule_colour, linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = matrix), colour = ink_colour, size = 2.6) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = matrix),
    data = top_panel_labels,
    vjust = -1,
    size = 4.2,
    family = report_font,
    colour = secondary_colour
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(CSF = 16, Serum = 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  # headroom above the top panel for the CSF and Serum labels
  scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.6, 1.2))) +
  labs(x = "Median share of samples above the LOD, per panel", y = NULL) +
  theme_slides(base_size = 14)
```

::: {.notes}
- **Linked:** the sample's subjid and visit day match a sampling visit. The analyses use each
  participant's earliest sample per matrix.
- **QC warnings:** the share of sample–panel pairs that Olink flagged.
- **Values below the LOD** are kept, as Olink advises, but assays detected in fewer than half of
  the samples are left out of the association screens (the red line).
- **CSF against serum:** CSF has far less protein than serum, so more CSF assays fall below the
  LOD.
:::

## Do plates or biology drive the protein data? {visibility="`r olink_visibility`"}

::: {.why}
**Why:** if samples cluster by assay plate, plate effects could pass for disease effects. The
main axes of variation should line up with biology (category, age), not with plates.
:::

```{r}
#| label: pca-figure
#| eval: !expr has_olink
#| fig-height: 4.6

# The first principal component against plate or group, one panel per
# matrix.
plot_first_component <- function(data, x, x_label, scales = "free_y") {
  ggplot(data, aes(x = {{ x }}, y = pc1)) +
    geom_jitter(
      width = 0.15,
      height = 0,
      size = 0.7,
      alpha = 0.6,
      colour = context_colour
    ) +
    summarise_median_iqr(linewidth = 0.7, size = 0.35) +
    facet_wrap(vars(matrix), ncol = 1, scales = scales) +
    labs(x = x_label, y = "First principal component") +
    theme_slides(base_size = 14)
}

# Plate IDs can be long, so plates are numbered within each matrix.
first_component_by_plate <- pca_scores |>
  mutate(plate_number = factor(dense_rank(plate)), .by = matrix) |>
  plot_first_component(
    plate_number,
    "Plate, numbered in ID order",
    scales = "free"
  )

first_component_by_group <- pca_scores |>
  drop_small_groups() |>
  plot_first_component(group, NULL) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = short_group_labels)

first_component_by_plate +
  first_component_by_group +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1.6)) &
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = paper_colour, colour = NA))
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| eval: !expr has_olink
batch_texts <- batch_summary |>
  mutate(across(c(plate, group, age), \(r_squared) round(r_squared, 2))) |>
  glue::glue_data("{matrix}: plate {plate}, category {group}, age {age}")
show_result(
  "Largest R² over the first five components: ",
  join_with_dots(batch_texts)
)
```

::: {.notes}
- **PCA:** run on the kept assays per matrix. Missing values are filled with the assay median,
  and every assay is scaled.
- **R²:** for each of the first five components, the share of its variance that plate, category,
  sex or age explain in a one-factor linear model. A plate R² near zero means the normalisation
  worked.
- **Age:** a large age R² is common in proteomics, which is why the later models adjust for age.
:::

## Which proteins differ between carriers and controls? {visibility="`r olink_visibility`"}

::: {.why}
**Why:** the most basic biomarker question is which proteins differ with the HD gene. Carriers
and controls differ in age and sex mix, so both are adjusted for.
:::

```{r}
#| label: volcano-figure
#| eval: !expr has_olink
#| fig-height: 4.6
volcano_data <- differential |>
  mutate(significant = p_fdr < settings$fdr)

strongest_proteins <- volcano_data |>
  filter(significant) |>
  slice_min(p.value, n = 8, by = matrix)

ggplot(volcano_data, aes(x = estimate, y = -log10(p.value))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = rule_colour, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = significant), size = 0.9, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_text_repel(
    aes(label = assay),
    data = strongest_proteins,
    size = 4,
    family = report_font,
    colour = accent_colour,
    segment.colour = rule_colour,
    max.overlaps = 20
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(`FALSE` = context_colour, `TRUE` = ink_colour)
  ) +
  facet_wrap(vars(matrix), scales = "free") +
  labs(
    x = "Difference in NPX (log2), carriers minus controls",
    y = "−log10 p"
  ) +
  theme_slides(base_size = 15)
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| eval: !expr has_olink
differential_texts <- str_glue(
  "{differential_counts$matrix}: {differential_counts$higher} higher and ",
  "{differential_counts$lower} lower of ",
  "{format_number(differential_counts$tested)} (FDR {settings$fdr}); ",
  "strongest {differential_counts$strongest}"
)
show_result(join_with_dots(differential_texts))
```

::: {.notes}
- **Model:** one linear model per protein, NPX ~ carrier + age + sex. Carriers are hdcat 1–5
  with CAG ≥ 40; controls are hdcat 6; incomplete penetrance is left out.
- **Multiple testing:** p-values are corrected per matrix with Benjamini–Hochberg. Black points
  pass the false discovery rate.
- **Reading the x-axis:** NPX is log2, so a difference of 1 means twice as much.
- **Status:** this is a screen. Hits need replication, ideally with an absolute assay.
:::

## Which proteins track cUHDRS in carriers? {visibility="`r olink_visibility`"}

::: {.why}
**Why:** proteins that follow clinical severity *within* carriers are candidates for monitoring
progression. Age drives both protein levels and cUHDRS, so the correlation is adjusted for age
(and sex).
:::

```{r}
#| label: cuhdrs-proteins-table
#| eval: !expr has_olink
cuhdrs_associations |>
  slice_max(abs(rho), n = 8, by = matrix) |>
  mutate(q_value = format_p(p_fdr)) |>
  select(matrix, assay, panel, rho, q_value) |>
  gt(groupname_col = "matrix", rowname_col = "assay") |>
  cols_label(panel = "Panel", rho = "Partial ρ", q_value = "q (FDR)") |>
  fmt_number(rho, decimals = 2) |>
  style_table(font_size = 18)
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| eval: !expr has_olink
association_texts <- str_glue(
  "{cuhdrs_counts$matrix}: {cuhdrs_counts$passing} of ",
  "{format_number(cuhdrs_counts$tested)} proteins pass the FDR ",
  "({format_n(cuhdrs_counts$carriers)} carriers)"
)
show_result(join_with_dots(association_texts))
```

::: {.notes}
- **Method:** partial Spearman correlation. Rank the protein, cUHDRS and age, regress the rank
  of age and sex out of both, then correlate the residuals. Benjamini–Hochberg is applied per
  matrix.
- **Sign:** a negative ρ means more protein goes with a lower (worse) cUHDRS.
- **Interpretation:** these are associations at one time point, not evidence that a protein
  predicts decline.
:::

## Does serum reflect CSF? {visibility="`r pair_visibility`"}

::: {.why}
**Why:** blood is far easier to collect than CSF. Proteins whose serum levels follow their CSF
levels could be measured in blood. Proteins that don't need CSF.
:::

```{r}
#| label: csf-serum-figure
#| eval: !expr has_both_matrices
#| fig-height: 4.4
positive_control_rho <- csf_serum |>
  filter(assay == positive_control) |>
  slice_head(n = 1)

lowest_break <- floor(min(csf_serum$rho) * 4) / 4

ggplot(csf_serum, aes(x = rho)) +
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 0.025,
    boundary = 0,
    fill = context_colour,
    colour = paper_colour
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = positive_control_rho$rho,
    colour = accent_colour,
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = positive_control_rho$rho,
    y = Inf,
    label = positive_control,
    vjust = 1.5,
    hjust = -0.15,
    family = report_font,
    size = 4.5,
    colour = accent_colour
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(-1, 1, by = 0.25),
    limits = c(lowest_break, 1)
  ) +
  labs(x = "CSF–serum Spearman correlation, per protein", y = "Proteins") +
  theme_slides()
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| eval: !expr has_both_matrices
strongly_correlated <- sum(csf_serum$rho > strong_correlation)
show_result(
  str_glue("{format_number(nrow(csf_serum))} proteins; median correlation "),
  str_glue("{format_number(median(csf_serum$rho), digits = 2)}; "),
  str_glue("{format_number(strongly_correlated)} above {strong_correlation}.")
)
```

::: {.notes}
For each protein kept in both matrices, the Spearman correlation is taken across participants
with both a CSF and a serum sample, if at least 10 have both. Proteins made in the brain and
leaking to blood (such as NfL) tend to correlate; proteins made mainly in blood often don't.
:::

## A positive check: neurofilament light {visibility="`r olink_visibility`"}

::: {.why}
**Why:** NfL is the best-established fluid marker of neurodegeneration in HD (Byrne et al.
2017). If it does not rise across categories and fall with cUHDRS, suspect the data linkage
before the biology.
:::

```{r}
#| label: nefl-figure
#| eval: !expr has_olink
#| fig-height: 6
nefl_carriers <- nefl |>
  filter(carrier, !is.na(cuhdrs))

if (nrow(nefl) > 0) {
  nefl_by_group <- nefl |>
    drop_small_groups() |>
    plot_strip_by_group(npx) +
    facet_wrap(vars(matrix), scales = "free_y") +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = short_group_labels) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "NPX") +
    theme_slides(base_size = 13)

  nefl_by_cuhdrs <- ggplot(nefl_carriers, aes(x = cuhdrs, y = npx)) +
    geom_point(colour = ink_colour, size = 0.8, alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_smooth(
      method = "loess",
      formula = y ~ x,
      se = FALSE,
      colour = accent_colour,
      linewidth = 0.8
    ) +
    facet_wrap(vars(matrix), scales = "free_y") +
    labs(x = "cUHDRS (carriers)", y = "NPX") +
    theme_slides(base_size = 13)

  (nefl_by_group / nefl_by_cuhdrs) &
    theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = paper_colour, colour = NA))
}
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
#| eval: !expr has_olink
nefl_associations <- cuhdrs_associations |>
  filter(assay == positive_control)

if (nrow(nefl_associations) > 0) {
  nefl_texts <- nefl_associations |>
    mutate(rho = format_number(rho, digits = 2)) |>
    glue::glue_data("{matrix} {rho}")
  show_result("NEFL partial ρ with cUHDRS: ", join_with_dots(nefl_texts))
}
```

::: {.notes}
NEFL is Olink's assay for neurofilament light. If it is missing from the export, these plots
stay empty. If NfL looks flat across categories on a real release, check the sample-to-visit
linkage first.
:::

# Summary

## What the first look shows

```{r}
#| results: asis
median_red_cells <- median(csf_collections$erythrocytes, na.rm = TRUE)

summary_lines <- c(
  str_glue(
    "- **Data:** {format_n(n_distinct(pds$profile$subjid))} participants and ",
    "{format_n(nrow(pds$participation))} packages; ",
    "{format_percent(single_package_share)} have one package, so the data are ",
    "mostly cross-sectional."
  ),
  str_glue(
    "- **cUHDRS:** complete for {format_n(nrow(source_visits))} packages; ",
    "medians by category: {describe_group_medians(cuhdrs_first, cuhdrs)}."
  ),
  str_glue(
    "- **Tracks burden:** Spearman correlation with CAP in carriers ",
    "{format_number(cap_rho, digits = 2)}."
  ),
  str_glue(
    "- **CSF quality:** median {format_number(median_red_cells, digits = 1)} ",
    "red cells per µl."
  )
)

if (has_olink) {
  passing_differential <- str_glue(
    "{differential_counts$matrix} ",
    "{differential_counts$higher + differential_counts$lower}"
  )
  passing_cuhdrs <- str_glue("{cuhdrs_counts$matrix} {cuhdrs_counts$passing}")
  summary_lines <- c(
    summary_lines,
    str_glue(
      "- **Olink, carriers against controls:** proteins passing the FDR: ",
      "{str_flatten_comma(passing_differential)}."
    ),
    str_glue(
      "- **Olink, cUHDRS in carriers:** proteins passing the FDR: ",
      "{str_flatten_comma(passing_cuhdrs)}."
    )
  )
}

cat(summary_lines, sep = "\n")
```

::: {.notes}
Every number on this slide is computed at render time from the release the deck was built on.
:::

## Limitations

- **Mostly cross-sectional.** Few participants have repeat packages, over short spans.
- **A selected sample.** Exclusions for anticoagulants, high CRP, recent investigational drugs
  and LP risk make HDClarity healthier than Enroll-HD overall.
- **Category is carried forward.** hdcat is reviewed only at screenings 1 and 5, so it can lag
  behind the current stage.
- **Relative proteomics.** NPX compares samples within an assay, not absolute concentrations or
  levels across assays.
- **Screens, not tests.** Thousands of models, corrected for FDR, generate hypotheses to
  replicate.

::: {.notes}
These limits follow from the study design and the data type; they are not specific to any one
release.
:::

## Possible next steps

- **Adjust for disease burden:** model proteins against cUHDRS with CAP or HD-ISS in the model,
  to separate disease burden from age.
- **Test–retest reliability:** use the repeat sampling visits (4–8 weeks apart) to measure the
  reliability of the top proteins.
- **Blood contamination:** run sensitivity analyses that exclude or adjust for heavily
  contaminated CSF samples.
- **Replicate the hits:** in the SomaScan data or with targeted assays.
- **Plan longitudinal analyses:** as more participants accumulate repeat packages.

::: {.notes}
These are suggestions for discussion, ordered from quickest to most work.
:::
